+This is an initial subset of the SQL:2016 `JSON_OBJECT` constructor. It supports the key/value
+members, the value-level `FORMAT JSON` marker, the `{ NULL | ABSENT } ON NULL` clause, and a
+string-type `RETURNING`. The following SQL/JSON clauses are not yet supported:
+* The `{ WITH | WITHOUT } UNIQUE KEYS` clause. Duplicate keys are kept in source order (the
+  `WITHOUT UNIQUE KEYS` behavior); there is no option to reject them.
+* `RETURNING` to a non-string type, or with a binary/`FORMAT JSON` output clause. The result is
+  always JSON text of a string type.

+    An expression producing a member name. It must be a non-null string; a `NULL` key raises an
+    error at runtime. The key is validated before the `ON NULL` handling, so a `NULL` key raises the
+    error even when the member's value is `NULL` and `ABSENT ON NULL` would otherwise omit it.
+    In the `key : value` form, the first top-level `:` after the key ends it, so a `:` extraction
+    key must be parenthesized and cast to a string (an extraction yields a `VARIANT`):
+    An expression producing the member value. Values may have different types and may be nested
+    JSON constructors. `JSON_OBJECT()` with no members produces the empty object `{}`. A value is
+    spliced in as raw JSON, rather than quoted as a string, only when it carries `FORMAT JSON` (see
+    below) -- either the explicit clause or the implicit form carried by a recognized JSON producer
+    written directly in the value position. This covers a nested `JSON_OBJECT` or `JSON_ARRAY` (e.g.
+    `JSON_OBJECT('a' VALUE JSON_OBJECT('b' VALUE 1))` produces `{"a":{"b":1}}`), and a nested
+    `JSON_QUERY` under the default `KEEP QUOTES`, which returns JSON text (e.g.
+    `JSON_QUERY` with `OMIT QUOTES` returns an ordinary string, so it is quoted like any other value
+    `{"n":"Ada"}`). Without `FORMAT JSON`, an ordinary string value is always quoted, even when its
+    contents are themselves valid JSON text (e.g. `JSON_OBJECT('a' VALUE '{"b":1}')` produces
+    `{"a":"{\"b\":1}"}`). Implicit raw splicing applies to the direct syntax above and to the
+    unqualified comma form (e.g. `json_object('a', json_object('b', 1))`, which carries the nested
+    producer through to the built-in and produces `{"a":{"b":1}}`). A qualified or otherwise generic

+    Marks a string `value` as already-JSON text, so it is spliced into the object verbatim instead
+    of being quoted (e.g. `JSON_OBJECT('a' VALUE '{"b":1}' FORMAT JSON)` produces `{"a":{"b":1}}`).
+    A nested JSON constructor written directly in the value position carries `FORMAT JSON`
+    implicitly. `FORMAT JSON` requires a string argument (an untyped `NULL` literal is also accepted
+    and follows the `ON NULL` behavior). At runtime, a non-null `FORMAT JSON` value must contain
+    exactly one well-formed JSON value; malformed text or multiple top-level values raise an error.
+    How to handle a member whose `value` is `NULL`:
+    * `NULL ON NULL` (the default) keeps the member with a JSON `null` value.
+    * `ABSENT ON NULL` omits the member entirely.
+    The type of the result. It must be a string type; the result is JSON text. If `RETURNING` is
+    omitted, the result type is `STRING`. `CHAR` / `VARCHAR` are normalized to `STRING` (the length
+    is not enforced, because the fragment is serialized directly).
+-- Construct an object from key/value pairs
+-- KEY before the member name is also accepted
+SELECT json_object(KEY 'id' VALUE 7, KEY 'name' VALUE 'Ada') AS obj;
+-- The `:` separator is equivalent to VALUE; NULL ON NULL (the default) keeps null members
+-- Comma-separated key/value pairs are also accepted
+-- ABSENT ON NULL omits members whose value is NULL
+SELECT json_object('id' : 7, 'v' : NULL ABSENT ON NULL) AS obj;
+-- A nested JSON_OBJECT composes and is spliced in raw
+SELECT json_object('a' VALUE json_object('b' VALUE 1)) AS obj;
+-- FORMAT JSON splices an already-JSON string verbatim instead of quoting it
+SELECT json_object('a' VALUE '{"b":1}' FORMAT JSON) AS obj;

+ * Renders a JSON_OBJECT value by writing every member into one [[JacksonGenerator]] lifecycle,
+ * rather than serializing each member separately and splicing the fragments. Shared by the
+ * `evaluate` takes a carrier row of the already-evaluated members flattened as

+ * key raises JSON_OBJECT_NULL_KEY before its value is evaluated. Per member it writes the field
+ * name then the value -- a raw (`FORMAT JSON`) value spliced verbatim (validated first when it is
+ * arbitrary user text), a null written as JSON `null` or dropped under ABSENT ON NULL, any other
+ * value rendered through the shared generator's type writer.
